details: The best possible method is to use the spinning wheel on the of Lumbridge Castle, and to bank on the . A full load of 28 wool takes approximately 50 seconds to convert into balls of wool. Travel and banking time is ~20 seconds in between loads. You should use a preset with wool in your inventory to speed up the process.

location: Edgeville Dungeon hill giant resource dungeon
details:
There are 4 spawns of limpwurt root in the resource dungeon located within Edgeville Dungeon where the Hill Giants are. To access the dungeon efficiently, a brass key is needed to enter the hut just west of Cooks' Guild. Then, head south to the room containing Hill Giants and limpwurt root spawns.

As they are level 26, Hill Giants are aggressive to any player with a combat level of 52 or less, which may be an annoyance to the gathering process. It is therefore recommended to have at least level 53 combat. 

On an averagely populated world, each limpwurt root re-spawns at a rate of around 56 seconds. However, as it takes less than 15 seconds to collect all 4 roots, it is recommended to constantly switch between worlds, effectively eliminating the respawn time. Once the inventory is full, head back up the shortcut to Varrock and bank the limpwurt roots at the Grand Exchange. Use of Surge will allow the player to make faster trips.

The profit rate assumes kills per hour. Your actual profits may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

Chickens can be killed at Fred the Farmer's farm, just north of the Lumbridge Market and its bank chest. It's important to use area loot for this method. Chickens drop raw chicken, feathers, and bones. The bones should be bound to your action bar to quickly bury it for prayer experience. The other items should be banked and then sold. There are also 3 egg spawns in the area, and chickens can lay eggs, which can be sold on the Grand Exchange for  coins, and raw chicken can be sold for  coins. Feathers are dropped in quantities of 5 or 15 at a time and sells for  each.

As chickens have very few life points, a fast hitting weapon such as a scimitar is recommended for melee. For magic it's recommended to use a staff of air for an unlimited supply of air runes; abilities like Dragon Breath allow you to kill several chickens at once. One run could be completed in a minute with intense focus. There are 8 chicken spawns in the coop; if you kill all of them fast enough you have a few seconds before you can kill the second wave, after which you should have enough eggs and raw chicken to bank (the ratio may vary, this assumes 12 eggs to 15 raw chickens).

Close the door to Fred's house to prevent chickens from wandering in, making it harder to kill them and collect drops (being inside also causes you to pick up unwanted shears by area loot). Consider closing the gate as well when you are leaving for the bank to prevent them from wandering outside. All the chickens always respawn in the coop area.

If this spot is busy, there are other chicken coops on the road to Varrock, and in the farm just south of Falador.

The profit rate assumes kills per hour. Your actual profits may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

Level 2 cows in Burthorpe have 25 life points and always drop cowhide. The pen is located south of the Burthorpe lodestone. Start killing the cows - they will respawn instantly. Since they have a fairly long death animation, begin by killing multiple cows before looting the first cow's hide. This is faster than waiting for the first one to finish dying. Once you have 28 cowhides, click on Tanya Hyde, who is inside the pen. She will tan the hides into hard leather for 3 coins each, or soft leather, whichever is cheaper. Run north to the Bank Gnome, bank the leather, run back to the cow pen, and repeat.

For players who intend to use either Magic or Ranged, it is highly recommended to equip a weapon with decent accuracy and does not use ammunition (E.g. Mindspike, Chargebow, Quickbow). Players with sufficient Magic or Ranged levels may use Dragon Breath
(5 Magic), (Chain (45 Magic), or Ricochet (45 Ranged) in order to kill more cows.

At times it may be better to make soft leather instead - hard leather is currently worth, while soft leather is currently worth.

location: North of Cairn Isle, near Shilo VillageGraahk location.png
details:
Graahks can be found north of Cairn Island, in Karamja, and are easily accessibly via the fairy ring code . They are hunted using a teasing stick and pitfall trapping with logs and a knife.

At level 41 Hunter, the graahks will commonly jump over your pitfall traps, so 60+ Hunter is recommended to reduce the time it takes to capture a graahk. A set of Larupia hunter gear may also improve catch rates.

When captured, graahks will yield either a graahk fur or a tatty graahk fur. The exact ratio of tatty to perfect furs vary with your Hunter level. The latter should be discarded, as it's only worth coins, but the perfect furs are worth  coins.

location: Grand Exchange or bank chest recommended
details:
Avantoe are in high demand to create Super energy and Extreme attacks. It is often profitable to clean the grimy herbs and sell them on the Grand Exchange. Like all methods involving large amounts of buying and selling, it is recommended to test the market first to make sure cleaning avantoe is profitable.

28 herbs can be cleaned per inventory, and each inventory takes 16.8s (28 ticks), so a maximum of around 5,000 herbs can be cleaned per hour. Due to the risk of repetitive strain, it is advised to use make-x to speed up the cleaning process.

Utilising a Herblore cape, presets, and the action bar, it is possible to clean an inventory approximitely every two seconds resulting in up to 50,000 herbs cleaned per hour.

Please note that grimy avantoes have a buying limit of 10,000 every four hours, so you may clean them faster than you can buy them.

This guide assumes kills per hour. Your profit per hour may vary depending on your speed.

Blue dragons, found in the Taverley blue dragon resource dungeon, always drop dragon bones and blue dragonhide (along with many other chance drops), which sell for  and  respectively. This makes each kill worth 0 coins. 

The usage of a beast of burden such as a war tortoise allows for up to 23 kills per trip. Each trip will require about 1.5 minutes to bank hides and bones and return to the resource dungeon. The closest bank is just south of the Taverley lodestone and is very close to the entrance to the Taverley dungeon. With 70 Agility, the Agility shortcut to the blue dragon lair may be used, and running from the Taverley bank to the resource dungeon takes less than 1 minute. Banking time will approximately triple if the Agility shortcut is not used. If players find waiting for the Home Teleport too tedious, they can also use the Falador shortcut (West of the Western bank in Falador). Simply teleport with Falador Teleport tabs.

With at least 60 Dungeoneering, it is possible to enter the Taverley blue dragon resource dungeon, which is seldom crowded. Kills per hour may be maximised by picking up drops in rotation. It takes a few seconds for each dragon's drops to appear after being killed, so it is advisable to pick up the drops only after coming back to the same spot. Additionally, the number of kills per hour may be increased at level 85 Herblore by making super antifire potions, allowing the use of two-handed and dual-wield weapons.

Players with 68 Divination should consider making signs of the porter IV. Porters can send any picked up blue dragonhides to the bank, allowing you to carry more bones per trip. IV is recommend due to being among the lowest cost per item teleport ( coins, assuming that all components are bought from the GE) and due to its 20 charge limit being comparable to a full inventory of bones plus a few miscellaneous drops. Porters will not activate on dragon bones however, but players can consider using magic notepaper on the bones or the pack-yak's winter storage special to extend their trip. Buying magic notepaper can cut into profits quite a bit, so players will have to determine whether or not the convenience is worth it to them.
You may also get more kills per hour by using legacy mode, however this isn't recommended for lower combat level players.

details:
The numbers listed assumes using expansive pouch, the Infinity ethereal outfit, and the Abyssal Titan, and running trips per hour while using the powerburst of sorcery every fourth trip. It also assumes that the player has completed the Elite Wilderness tasks to increase the magical thread chance.

With optimised dives and surges, one can expect around 112–138 trips an hour, while without using any mobility abilities, one can expect 90–105 trips an hour.

Using the expansive pouch, the Infinity ethereal outfit, and an Abyssal titan, you can hold up to 128 essence per trip, resulting in a profit of  coins per trip.

The Mage of Zamorak is located low-level wilderness, near the source of the River Lum. Make sure PvP is toggled off by talking to Vala in Edgeville. See Abyss for more information on how to navigate the abyss.

The suggested outfit is as follows (make sure enhanced excalibur has the Mobile perk and Wilderness sword is in the inventory):


A typical trip would look like:
# Open bank and load preset, or load last preset
# Run to wilderness wall (surge when you can do so in a straight line to the wall)
# Cross the wall
# Dive immediately after crossing the wall.
# Surge after passing the tree to go deeper into the wilderness
# Click on Zamorak mage to teleport (you can configure teleport to be the left-click option by right-clicking him and selecting configure)
# Go to the death portal.
# Drink a powerburst of sorcery if off cooldown, then craft the runes
# Teleport to Edgeville bank with the wilderness sword.
# Repeat from step 1.

The amount of death runes crafted increases at higher levels, up to about 30% at 99, due to the greater likelihood of crafting two runes per essence. Players can use Runecrafting potions to craft death runes without the level 65 requirement.

Completing Hero's Welcome allows the player to make 5% more runes. Players also have a chance of receiving magical thread (currently worth  coins each) while crafting runes via the Abyss.

Blue dragon scales spawn in the Taverley Dungeon and the Taverley blue dragon resource dungeon, and they are currently worth coins each. The better place to collect them is the resource dungeon as they're closer together and there are more of them, but that area requires 60 Dungeoneering to access. Without the resource dungeon, you can collect about 550 scales per hour, compared to 900 inside the resource dungeon. 70 Agility is also recommended to avoid having to traverse Taverley Dungeon, which would require a dusty key. A Beast of Burden like the spirit terrorbird, war tortoise, or pack yak are also very helpful to cut down on banking time.

Teleport to Taverley using the Taverley lodestone and head south to the dungeon entrance. Use Surge to travel faster. Enter the obstacle pipe if you have 70 Agility, or otherwise go the long way around (see Map:Taverley Dungeon for details). Enter the resource dungeon if you're able, and start collecting the dragon scales, being careful not to attack any blue dragons by accident. Pick up all of the scales (they respawn very quickly), storing them in your familiar as needed. Enabling area loot will allow you to pick up multiple scales quickly. When your inventory is full, teleport back to Taverley, bank the scales, and repeat. Grinding the scales is usually not worth the time taken and is not recommended, as the scale dust costs much less than the regular scales.

To avoid accidentally attacking blue dragons you can hide the option to attack. Do this by opening Settings > Gameplay Tab > Combat & Action Bar > 'Choose Option' Menu, then under the header NPC attack option use the pull-down menu to choose Hidden. While the attack option is hidden you'll be able to click through blue dragons to get the scales underneath them. This is especially helpful if you need to gather scales outside of the resource dungeon due to lack of access. Be aware this will hide your attack option on all NPC's, so be sure to change this back to the original setting of Combat Level instead of Hidden once you're done gathering the scales.

details:
Wine of Zamorak is used to create super ranging potions and super Zamorak brews. There is a wine of zamorak spawn that can be taken from the table in the Captured Temple by hand only if the six nearby Monks of Zamorak are dead, or by using Telekinetic Grab, which requires 33 Magic.

The temple is near the Falador lodestone - run north from here to reach it. Use Telekinetic Grab to take the wine. This will make the Monks of Zamorak aggressive, but running east past where Miazrqa wanders will immediately drop their aggro. Alternatively players may kill all the monks and then take the wine by hand. As the wine respawns every 30 seconds, players should hop worlds to obtain more. 

The nearby altar permits liberal use of Protect from Magic to prevent the player from taking too much damage from the monks. Once your inventory is full you can bank in Falador and repeat.

If you are able to world hop perfectly after each telekinetic grab you can obtain 120 per hour (a profit of ). This can be very difficult to do.

Use of a beast of burden such as spirit terrorbird or pack yak is recommended as it will increase the amount of time collecting wines per hour.

Charging water orbs map.png orbs are worth coins, and are created by casting Charge Water Orb on unpowered orbs at the Water Obelisk. With an equipped water staff, this requires 3 cosmic runes per cast (or 0 coins). Using a ring of duelling to teleport to Castle Wars (or the Tokkul-zo) for banking, you can charge 27 orbs per trip (one inventory slot is needed for the cosmic runes, unless you use a large rune pouch), resulting in a profit of 0 coins per trip (0 if using large rune pouch).

The Water Obelisk is located on an island in Catherby only accessible via the Taverley dungeon. Using the map on the right as a guide through the dungeon, the round trip to the obelisk, counting banking, takes approximately 185 seconds using the 80 agility shortcut, 205 seconds using the 70 agility shortcut, or 325 seconds without any shortcuts. 
If you have a Dungeoneering Cape you can use the teleport option to teleport to the Taverley Hellhound Dungeon which puts you within clickable range of the ladder to the Water Obelisk, this will considerably reduce travel time.

Bear in mind that running through the Taverley dungeon places you in combat range of aggressive black demons and poison spiders.

Assuming the unpowered orbs and cosmic runes are purchased, you can make 525 water orbs an hour using the level 80 agility shortcut, 475 water orbs using the level 70 agility shortcut , and 300 water orbs using no shortcuts.

Raw potatoes are the base ingredient for all types of potatoes with toppings. There is a consistent demand for raw potatoes on the Grand Exchange, and someone has to pick them!

Potatoes can be found in potato fields, and the best free-to-play location is north of the Lumbridge cow pen. Starting off at the Varrock lodestone, walk the road south, going through the fence. The potato field is directly to the south east. Use of Surge can reduce travel time.

Pick the potatoes - travelling diagonally along the rows is most effective. Members can store potatoes in sacks to reduce the amount of time spent banking, and increase profit earned per hour. Potato seeds are sometimes obtained from picking potatoes on members worlds; it is therefore recommended to do this method on a free to play world.

Teleport to the Burthorpe lodestone and bank there. Teleport back to the Varrock lodestone and run back to the potato field to continue picking potatoes.

location: Grand Exchange or bank chest recommended
details:
Snapdragon potion (unfinished) are used to create super restores. Because these are often used to train Herblore, and adding clean snapdragon to a vial of water gives little experience, many players avoid the tedium of making unfinished potions and buy them directly from the Grand Exchange. 

Using portable wells gives a 5% chance of making an extra potion and the scroll of cleansing gives a permanent 10% chance of not using up an ingredient when making potions. The bonuses of these two items increase the number of unfinished potions you can make, and the portable well also makes the process less click-intensive. With a portable well placed next to a bank chest, click on the bank chest and deposit your inventory and withdraw 14 herbs and 14 vials of water by using a bank preset, and repeat.

There is usually a portable well placed and maintained by someone else next to the bank chest in the Lumbridge Market in world 84. However, if there isn't one and no-one else provides one within a reasonable amount of time, you may have to use your own wells. Assuming the portable wells are bought at Grand Exchange prices, this will cost coins per hour. 2,310 Snapdragon potions can be made on an average raising the money per hour to.

location: Grand Exchange or bank chest recommended
details:
Raw summer pies are used to quickly train Cooking and Magic by using the Bake Pie spell. They are made by using the ingredients (Strawberry, Watermelon, Cooking apple) on a Pie shell, in that order. 

To avoid losing money, test out the profit of making one pie before you do them in bulk.

# Buy an equal number of pie shells, strawberries, watermelons and cooking apples from the Grand Exchange (each has a buying limit of 1,000 per four hours)
# Withdraw 14 pie shells and 14 strawberries, and use one on the other. This will bring up a menu to make part summer pies, click make-all
# Once you've made 14, bank them and repeat
# When all of your strawberries and pie shells are gone, use all of your watermelons on the part summer pies
# Then use the cooking apples on the part summer pies (watermelon) to create raw summer pies. 

Adding an ingredient 14 times will take about 20 seconds including banking, so you can make up to 840 raw summer pies per hour.

The profit rate assumes kills per hour. Your actual profits may be higher or lower depending on your speed and luck.

Nechryael are found on the top floor of the Morytania Slayer tower and always drop infernal ashes, worth 0 coins each. Level 80 Slayer is required to harm and are reasonably weak for their level. Approximately 386 can be killed per hour at higher levels (counting banking times, assuming a ring of slaying is used for teleporting to the Slayer tower and the desert amulet or TokKul-zo is used for banking). Nechryael can randomly summon two death spawns that drop accursed ashes worth 0. With AoE attacks, they can be easily killed with little attention paid. Strong melee armour is advised, and for low level players it is recommended to take food for healing. Higher level players may wish to use Turmoil and/or Soul Split for healing which will drastically increase the number of kills per hour. If using the desert amulet to bank, there is an altar close to the teleport location to recharge Prayer points.

With the Death Note relic, ashes are automatically noted, making banking unnecessary and increasing kills per hour significantly. Using an aggression potion with this combination results in a very AFK moneymaking method. 

It is also possible to obtain a Slayer contract from Markus, located just outside of the Slayer Tower entrance. By completing a contract of 180 kills, he will reward you 109,000 coins. This alone results in a profit of up to  coins per hour at the given kills per hour. Alternatively, it is possible to claim experience rewards from Markus instead of coins.

In addition to the profit earned from drops and Slayer contracts, Nechryael also drop medium plated rune salvages and various herb seeds. However, it is not recommended to pick items up that are worth less than infernal ashes as it would lower the profit per hour. Bringing a spring cleaner 2000 or above will automatically convert the salvage to coins (high alch value).

Headless arrows are made by using feathers on arrow shafts, and they are used in Fletching to create arrows for quick experience gains. Because most fletchers will not create the headless arrows on their own, there is an opportunity for low-level players to make a fair amount of profit (and decent experience) by fletching headless arrows.

To start with, test the profit of making one headless arrow -- buy one feather and one arrow shaft from the Grand Exchange, make a headless arrow, and sell it. If the profit is less than 10, there may be better options to make money. If it is higher, buy up feathers and arrow shafts in bulk. It may be more profitable to purchase or even chop logs to make the shafts, however that would also require additional time.

To create headless arrows you need the arrow shafts and feathers in your inventory. Left click on the arrow shafts, then click "Fletch" (or space bar) to make 60 sets of 15 arrow shafts automatically, taking about 72 seconds. You can make 45,000 headless arrows an hour if you have enough materials. However, feathers and arrow shafts have a buying limit of 100,000 every four hours, so you can only buy about 130 minutes worth of headless arrow materials per four hours. It may be useful to put in an overnight offer for feathers and arrow shafts if you have enough money to start with. You can buy more feathers at fishing shops (around 1,000 per 24 hours per shop).

Because making headless arrows does not require banking and only takes up three inventory spaces, it can be used in conjunction with other moneymaking methods where there is a long wait between actions. This includes collecting cave nightshade, cave goblin wire, and potato cactus. For F2P players, Grapes at the Cooks' Guild or Red spiders eggs  in the Varrock Sewers can be good.

To find the current location of a Portable fletcher, ask in the "portables" Friends chat.

Polar kebbit hunting is one of the best money making method for a level 1 hunter until level 29, when one can hunt green salamanders. This method is just as effective at level 1 as at level 99, and only depends on the familiarity of the player with the routes of the kebbit, so it is worth the time to take time to read through this whole guide for tips if you are unfamiliar with hunting Polar kebbits.

About 105 kebbits may be hunted in one hour by using the Hunting Area in Taverley. On banking runs, it is recommended to use the lodestone teleport to save 1 or two seconds on the run from the bank to the hunting area, and also giving you time to rest. Each inventory should consist of 26 Polar kebbit fur as each kill will give 3 drops, meaning you will be forced to drop items to make the kill. Bones should be buried in pairs instead of after every kill as 2 bones can be buried in one animation. The raw beast meat should be dropped while examining one of the rocks to save time as it holds no true monetary value.

To start each route, search one of the 2 burrows ("hole") located at the north and south ends of the hunting area. Tracks will appear, which will lead to set places. Click on a rock close to the end of the tracks that you speculate the next set of track will lead to. Without memorizing every pattern, there are several ways to easily identify/narrow down the rocks the kebbit passes by. 
:1. The kebbit track will never cross over the original tracks like a + sign. It may overlap, but never crosses over.
:2. After the second set of tracks has been found, the next tracks will have to lead to a snow drift, and only the two on the east and western side of the hunting area.
:3. The tracks don't double back.
:4. The rocks that will have fur on them will always be close to the end of the tracks.

details:
Raw wild pies are made by using the ingredients (Raw bear meat, Raw chompy, Raw rabbit) on a Pie shell, in that order. To avoid losing money, test out the profit of making one pie before you do them in bulk.

Buy an equal number of pie shells and ingredients from the Grand Exchange (each has a buying limit of 1,000 per four hours). Withdraw 14 pie shells and 14 raw bear meat, and use one on the other. This will bring up a menu to make part wild pies, so click to make-all. Once you've made 14, bank them and repeat. When all of your raw bear meat and pie shells are gone, use the raw chompy on the part wild pies in the same fashion, and then use the raw rabbit on the part wild pies (raw chompy) to create raw wild pies. Adding an ingredient 14 times will take about 20 seconds including banking, so you can make up to 840 raw wild pies per hour.

You can then sell the pies on the Grand Exchange. To maximise your profit, buy one raw wild pie at the instant price, and then sell all of yours for slightly below that price.

location: Grand Exchange or bank chest recommended
details:
Fellstalk potion (unfinished) are used to create Prayer renewals. Because these are often used to train Herblore, and adding clean fellstalk to a vial of water gives little experience, many players avoid the tedium of making unfinished potions and buy them directly from the Grand Exchange.

Using portable wells gives a 5% chance of making an extra potion and the scroll of cleansing gives a permanent 10% chance of not using up an ingredient when making potions. The bonuses of these two items increase the number of unfinished potions you can make, and the portable well also makes the process less click-intensive. With a portable well placed next to a bank chest, click on the bank chest and deposit your inventory and withdraw 14 herbs and 14 vials of water by using a bank preset, and repeat.

There is usually a portable well placed and maintained by someone else next to the bank chest in the Lumbridge Market in world 84. However, if there isn't one and no-one else provides one within a reasonable amount of time, you may have to use your own wells. Assuming the portable wells are bought at Grand Exchange prices, this will cost coins per hour. 2,310 Fellstalk potions can be made on an average raising the money per hour to.

details:
Soft clay is often used by players training Crafting or making urns who do not have the time to collect wet clay themselves.

One can cast Humidify on an inventory of clay to turn them into soft clay. Use astral runes and equip a steam battlestaff to maximise profit and efficiency. Set up one of your "Quick Presets" to Withdraw 27 clay and an astral rune, cast the Humidify spell, which will cause the whole inventory to turn into soft clay, open the bank, Click the Quick Preset and repeat. When playing at maximum efficiency, up to 400 spells can be cast per hour, for 10,800 clay.

By utilising bank preset, it can be done even faster resulting in more money and experience/hr. By setting the runes and raw clay as a quick preset, all you have to do is click the bank, click the preset, and click the humidify spell. This significantly lowers the click amount for this method.

The method above can be accelerated even further by binding Humidify to the same key as the quick preset. Click on the banker, press '1' (or 2, if that's what you chose), then '1' again.

Alternatively, casting Humidify vials may be profitable at an hour.

The outputs is approximate.

Puro-Puro is the choice spot to hunt implings as you are guaranteed to see large numbers of them at any given time. The most effective strategy involves snaring the target impling with a Bind spell then catching it while it is rendered immobile. The bind spell can only be cast when next to the target unless you are wielding a mainhand magic weapon. This will require you to swap to a staff/wand to snare then back to your net to catch the impling. To keep the rarer implings spawning, be sure to catch all implings that are higher-level than nature implings, including nature implings themselves.

Expect for the majority of the implings you see to be nature implings; magpies and zombies are approximately the same rarity; ninjas and pirates are significantly rarer. Dragon and Kingly implings are the rarest (thus the most valuable) appearing about 1 - 2 times an hour; it is possible to see more than 2 or none at all with no guarantees on appearances.

Wielding a magic butterfly net increases the catch rate on implings by 15%. As it is considered a magic weapon, it can be used to cast spells. Implings can only be bound by spells from the normal spellbook; ice does not work. Entangle, a level 79 spell, requires 3 nature runes to bind the target for 24 seconds.

Prior to catching implings, have enough impling jars on hand to stock at Elnock Inquisitor and buy the Imp repellent and jar generator. The repellent can be bought for three young, two gourmet and one earth impling jar. The jar generator can be bought for three essence, two eclectic and one nature impling jar. The jar generator can generate up to 33 impling jars per item; destroy it on the last charge. When it reaches 18 charges, immediately hunt the implings needed to rebuy it again.

It is also encouraged to enter from a Gielinor crop circle to gain the Farmer's affinity boost, which will significantly speed up powering through the wheat fields. The boost lasts for 30 minutes of in-game time.

A Fruit Bat scroll (Fruitfall) send the fruit bat foraging for fruit, and produces papayas, oranges, limes, pineapples and bananas. 

The most profitable and time-efficient of these is the papaya, which you will be collecting. The papaya is used in the creation of Adrenaline potions which are in high demand from pvmers.

Turn on Area loot in the options for faster and easier looting.

# Stand outside a bank with an open area near it - Edgeville and Clan Wars work well. 
# Summon your fruit bat, withdraw your stack of Fruit Bat scroll (Fruitfall)s, and bring two Summoning potions. 
# Start repeatedly using the fruitfall move - putting it on your action bar is helpful. When your special move points run out, drink a dose of the potion. You can use fruitfall 20 or 30 times, letting the fruit stack up near you.
# Collect all of the papayas (they should be on the top unless there are oranges) and bank them. 
# Repeat this indefinitely, occasionally withdrawing the bat's own foraged fruit, and summoning a new one when the familiar timer runs out.

The most efficient method is to set a key-bind to open the "area loot" feature in Settings > Controls > Action Bar to pick them up without moving.

Ruby harvests are the lowest level-requirement butterflies; however, they are also the highest in demand due to their use as the tertiary ingredient in a Forge regent pouch. At lower levels, it may be slightly difficult to catch any of these creatures; however at levels beyond 30, the catch rate is near 100%. With little input and short bank trips — which are even faster if the player invests in Phoenix Lair Teleports — ruby harvests provide for high hourly profit rates.

details:
Weapon poison++ is made by using cave nightshade on a vial of coconut milk and poison ivy berries. Cave nightshade only spawns inside the Skavid caves under Gu'Tanoth, east of Castle Wars, and is untradeable, so the spawn time of the nightshade is the limiting factor in how fast weapon poison++ can be made.
Cave nightshade locations.png
The easiest way to get there is by teleporting to the Yanille lodestone and walking to the most northern cave entrance marked on the map to the right. A skavid map is required to enter. A light source is required to prevent damage from swarming insects. Armoured gloves are required to pick cave nightshades. Cave nightshades can be noted with magic notepaper by using the nightshade on the paper, but not vice versa. Signs of the porter may also be used to bank the harvest.

It takes approximately 30 seconds for each of the plants to respawn (with a small amount of randomness), and both caves contain 7 plants. You can gather more quickly by hopping world rather than waiting for respawns.

The varanusaur envenomed perk gives a 10% chance to make 4 doses instead of 3 doses when mixing these potions.

The Superglass Make lunar spell can instantly turn an inventory full of sand and soda ash into molten glass. Withdraw sand and soda ash from your bank, activate Superglass Make, bank the resulting glass and repeat. On average 1.3 glass will be made for every sand-soda ash pair.

This can be done efficiently by using the same keybind for the bank preset and the spell on an action bar. For instance, using the first preset (keybind 1) and placing the Superglass Make spell on an action bar with the keybind 1 makes it possible to go through the crafting process by only pressing 1 and clicking the bank. This way it's possible to cast the spell about 2,000 times an hour.

Another, more click-intensive method is by positioning your camera so when you right click a bank chest or banker the cursor already is over the "Load last Preset from" option, and then almost immediately pressing the keybind for Superglass Make. Utilizing this method allows one cast of Superglass Make every Game tick, or 6,000 casts an hour assuming perfect uninterrupted timing.

The large or grasping rune pouch can be used to store Astral runes and then equipped, meaning you can convert 14 sets of sand and soda ash per cast instead of only 13, increasing the profit per hour by about 7%. The Elemental battlestaff supplies unlimited fire and air runes, further increasing profit.

Note that the buy limit for both buckets of sand and soda ashes on the Grand Exchange is 10,000 every four hours. It might be necessary to stock up beforehand to reach the output quantities shown on this guide.

details:
Killing black dragons gives decent combat experience as well as steady money in the form of their 100% drops, dragon bones and black dragonhide. It is recommended to use a high level ranged weapon to kill these creatures as they are weak to bolts. Two-handed or dual-wield ranged weapons may be used in conjunction with a super antifire potions to avoid dragonfire damage. A cheaper alternative with would be to use a regular antifire potion combined with protect from magic prayers, this negates damage taken highly, although food (Monkfish or better) is almost a necessity. Using an anti-dragon or dragonfire shield instead may reduce the profit. Additionally, beast of burden familiars will increase the number of kills possible between bank trips.

Consider using signs of the porter from divination to bank the dragonhides, it might boost your profit/hour due to less bank effort/more banks with the pack yak special move. Players with pack yak and Porter V will be able to kill up to 250 black dragons per hour.

One of the best places to kill black dragons is the Evil Chicken's Lair, accessed from Zanaris. This spot is rarely crowded. You need to use a raw chicken on the shrine in front of it to enter (kill one of the chickens running around the area). It's easy to bank from there, either walking to Zanaris or using a TokKul-Zo to teleport to the Fight Caves, bank, and use the fairy ring to return. If wearing a portent to the Lair, it should be noted that the portent WILL bank the raw chicken you pick up from killing one of the chickens. Unequipping the portent is necessary if obtaining a raw chicken in this manner.

other: Uncapped Potential Perk from Player Owned Farms
details:
Collecting mort myre fungi is very profitable as it is the secondary ingredient for making super energy potions. While wearing Morytania legs, players will receive double the amount of fungi when collecting. However, make sure there are at least two inventory spaces when collecting, otherwise players will only receive one fungus. Casting bloom affects rotting objects in the 8 squares around the player and consumes between 10 and 60 prayer points (though if the player only has 1 prayer point left, bloom can still be cast). Players should use a location surrounded by 3 rotting logs to increase the chances of obtaining mort myre fungus. An Ivandis flail or blessed silver sickle can be placed on the action bar to cast bloom with hotkeys. Using the action bar, you can increase your profit up to 2,500~ fungus, for an approximation of, by being tick-efficient. Players should use the three logs south of the Deposit Box as those are the most efficient. Gathering the fungus by prioritising the logs in the order of South-west, west, then East, you can cast bloom as soon as the mushrooms on the east log disappears, even though your character doesn't appear to be in the center yet. If the fungus on the logs disappears, it indicates that your character has reached that point even if it isn't shown. Using this, you will increase your fungus output by a decent amount. Additionally, you don't need to wait for the bloom effect to end, you can begin harvesting as soon as the stars start to fall and dim.

While harvesting Mort myre fungus, you may rarely receive a Gloomshroom zygomite (unchecked) which sells for .

Inventory setup should include 3 Prayer renewal (4) or 2 Prayer renewal flask (6), as 10 doses will be consumed in 1 hour. Each renewal dose will recover prayer points over 6 minutes, though as long as the potion effect is active bloom can be cast indefinitely. Super prayer renewal potion (6) can sometimes be cheaper per dose, having the same duration. As of right now, each Super prayer renewal potion dose is  cheaper than a Prayer renewal dose and  cheaper than a Prayer renewal flask dose.


If you have completed Deadliest Catch, you will have unlocked a deposit chest along the eastern banks of the River Salve. A short distance south of this, shown in the picture on the right, are 3 rotting logs within a 3  3 area. Simply cast bloom, collect, and deposit until you run out of prayer renewal doses. Using the bank deposit chest, this method increases your Mort myre fungi output considerably as it removes the need to bank every inventory; you now only have to bank once after the hour.

You can also increase the amount of fungi through the use of Farm totems on the Player-owned Farm. The Zygomite perk gives a 7% chance to give another mushroom when you gather, at tier one, and a 10% chance at tier two. This stacks with the Morytania legs buff, for a possible three fungi per harvest. Raising Zygomites requires 81 Farming, and the farm totems will only work if Elder Zygomites are in the Medium Pens.

For people that haven't completed Deadliest Catch: first, use the fairy ring network to teleport to . Run west until you see three rotting logs, as shown in the image above. Drink a dose of prayer renewal, stand in the middle of the 3 rotting logs and cast bloom. Mort myre fungi will not spawn every time. Always pick the northern log last because when picked, you will return to the middle, removing the need to click back. After a full inventory, teleport to the TzHaar Fight Cave with the TokKul-Zo to bank and repeat using the fairy ring just north. Alternatively, if you haven't got a TokKul-Zo, use the fairy ring to bank in Zanaris, although this is slightly slower.

Alternatively, players with 68 divination or greater can use sign of the porter IV to bank the fungus. This method will reduce the need for bank trips and increase the yield. Each sign of the porter will transport 20 fungi at a cost of  per charge. Profit per hour will be greater than that of banking at the TzHaar Fight Cave but be less than that of using the deposit chest due to the cost of porters.

Alternatively, players who complete the easy Ardougne achievements (Requires: Biohazard, Gertrude's Cat, Monk's Friend, Plague City, Tower of Life; 15  Fishing, 16  Thieving, 10  Construction), can use the Kandarin monastery Teleport after collecting fungi (but before banking with the TokKul-Zo ) to recharge their prayer point for free. The Kandarin monastery Teleport is a one click teleport spell that isn't interrupted by attacking ghasts unlike the TokKul-Zo. Return with a fairy ring as mentioned above.

location: Tower of Life (building), south-east of Ardougne
details:
The profit rate assumes kills per hour. Your actual profits may be higher or lower depending on your speed and luck.

Unicows may be killed for their 100% drop rate of unicorn horns, which are commonly used for both Herblore and Summoning. These creatures may be created in the Tower of Life by placing a unicorn horn and cowhide on the north-western altar. Unicows have a combat level of level 82 and attack using magic. Lower levelled players may wish to equip ranged armour, but food should not be necessary.

With an Ardougne cloak, the unicows have a chance of dropping noted unicorn horns instead, saving inventory space. Due to an update, this noted effect is permanently enabled and there is no way to disable it in order to guaranteed un-noted drops. However noted unicorn horn can be un-noted one at a time by either a right-click option on the Altar, or 'use' the horn on the Altar. With one unicorn horn and a war tortoise and inventory full of cowhides, it is possible to create and kill up to 45 unicows per trip. This will usually generate about 90 unicorn horns. Banking may be done via the fairy ring (code ). Returning to the Tower of Life may be done via the fairy ring once more or using the Ardougne cloak teleport to the Kandarin Monastery. Six or more trips per hour are feasible.

details:
White berries spawn location.png
Isafdar map.png
White berries spawn in an isolated area in Isafdar, north of the Tirannwn lodestone and just west of some light animica rocks. They respawn very quickly (about 4-5 seconds) after being picked up.

To get to the white berries area, use the Tirannwn lodestone, and click the red dot to the north on the minimap (your character will need to walk northwest then east to get around the trees). Consult the map above if you're unsure how to get there. It should take about 15 seconds to get to the berries from the lodestone. It's possible you'll take damage from the tripwires on the way, but the damage is generally insignificant and you'll be fully healed by the bank.

Once there, just stand over the white berry spawn, clicking it whenever they spawn. After you've collected 28 of them, use the TokKul-Zo to bank, and repeat. Each trip takes about three minutes for a profit of . Once you've got enough berries, sell them on the Grand Exchange.

It's also possible to use a Beast of Burden to increase the berries per trip. Using a pack yak, you could collect up to 600 berries per hour, for an hourly profit of .

As all you need to do is click once every few seconds, you can do other activities like High Level Alchemy or Disassemble on noted items while you wait.

details:
Utilising area loot and movement abilities, white berries may be collected at a faster volume than those found in Isafdar due to two berries spawning on Red Dragon Isle, though this may require more unlocks and attention. 

The Wilderness sword 1, which requires the Easy Wilderness achievements, is used to teleport to the Wilderness herb patch. You should utilise Dive and Surge to travel southeast to the agility shortcut on the southern end of Red Dragon Isle. Two hellhounds spawn near the agility shortcut, meaning you can utilise the Barge ability to path towards them if you are lacking in movement ability unlocks or if said abilities are on cooldown. The red dragons on the isle are not aggressive.

It is highly recommended to assign a keybind to the area loot interface through the controls tab in your settings. By doing this, it is possible to spam the keybind in order to remove the slight delay it will take for the white berries to show in the area loot interface once they spawn, allowing for quicker trips.

It is also highly suggested to stand one tile south of the southern white berries spawn, as this will prevent the nearby burnt bones from appearing in your area loot interface and ensure both spawns of berries will.

Once your inventory and familiar are full, teleport to War's Retreat or use the Wilderness sword to teleport to Edgeville. Deposit your berries and return to the Wilderness herb patch once more.

Fiyr Shades can be found at the end of the Shade Catacombs underneath Mort'ton. Accessing them requires a silver shade key, which is most easily obtained by burning Fiyr remains on the pyres to the southern part of Mort'ton (requiring 80 Firemaking and at least magic pyre logs), or burning Asyn remains, requiring 63 Firemaking and at least eucalyptus pyre logs. Use that key to enter the catacombs, going through the bronze, steel and silver doors.

There are four Fiyr Shades outside the rooms, and a few more inside them. You will be killing the four outside, and the room with two. Using your combat gear and abilities, quickly take down the shades. This should not be difficult as they have low defence and only 7000 LP. They will hardly hit you at all if you use ranged or magic as they only attack with melee. Wait for them to spawn, and repeat. On a highly populated world, this cycle could take less than 30 seconds. The remains are stackable in the inventory. They drop congealed blood occasionally. The shades are aggressive, so it's wise to have auto-retaliate on.
No food is needed, adrenaline, and an elite enhanced excalibur should be more than enough.

After you've gathered enough remains, sell them on the Grand Exchange. They shouldn't take too long to sell because they are used in invention and gold key chances. They offer pious components with a very low junk chance. Along with tortured souls, dropped by Edimmu, these remains are the only way to get gold keys, for gold chests. Gold chests are the only chests which can contain necromancer kits and shade skulls.

Teak pyre logs are made by combining 3 doses of sacred oil with teak logs. Each pyre log takes 1.2 seconds to make, setting a theoretical maximum of 3000 pyre logs per hour. However, accounting for time spent banking as well as human error and loss of attention, a more realistic figure would likely be roughly 2304 logs, or 144 inventories per hour - higher rates are possible, but hard to maintain.

Sacred oil has a buy limit of 1000 vials per 4 hours. To help get around this, you may want to buy 3-dose, 2-dose and 1-dose vials and decant them. details: Up to 2,500 magic pyre logs can be made per hour by combining four doses of sacred oil with magic logs. While 2,500 is the upper limit on the number of logs that can be made, 2,400 is a more realistic assumption. A major advantage of this method is that it may be performed at the Grand Exchange, allowing players to make even more money by merchanting at the same time. However, a disadvantage of this method is that only 1,000 bottles of sacred oil may be bought on the Grand Exchange every 4 hours. A further complication is that the 4-dose sacred oil is high in demand and low in supply, which makes the 3-dose oil much easier to obtain. Using 3-dose sacred oils decreases the amount of logs per inventory to 12, which in turn decreases profit-per-hour slightly. However, Buying 3-dose oils and having Bob Barter decant them into 4 doses is possible. Using this method also increases the buying limit to 1,750 4-dose oils per hour due to the extra 3,000 doses from 3-dose oils. Note that if you make the sacred oils yourself will increase your profit by several million as it only costs about 100k to make the necessary oils. This method will take several hours if on the official world.

After starting Zogre Flesh Eaters, you can loot ogre coffins by using ogre coffin keys on them. You'll often get random junk (bronze equipment, damaged armour), but about half the time you'll get zogre bones, and 10% of the time each you'll get raurg bones or fayrg bones. Ourg bones are especially rare, with about a 2% chance. Most of the profit from this method comes from the raurg bones, which are used for Daily Challenges and are far more expensive than any of the others.

Ogre coffin keys have a trade limit of 100 per four hours, and can be difficult to buy regardless. Consider stocking up on them before you begin.

To start this method, teleport to Castle Wars using a ring of duelling. Withdraw 25 or 26 ogre coffin keys from the bank, and walk south over the bridge and west around the rock wall to Jiggig. Hop over the crushed barricade, and run past the skogres and zogres to the three ogre coffins in the east.

Start opening the coffin -- just stay at one of them, it will close itself again before you can open a different coffin. Drop any unwanted junk you get, but keep on the lookout for grimy lantadyme in addition to the ancient bones. After you've used all your keys, teleport back to Castle Wars, bank, and run back to Jiggig. It takes six seconds for each coffin to open again, so a load of 26, plus banking time, is 200 seconds. This means that you could open 500 coffins per hour, getting on average 250 zogre bones, 50 raurg and fayrg bones, and 9 ourg bones.

After you've had enough, go to the Grand Exchange and sell your bones. The most important ones are again the raurg bones, -- they are fairly commonly traded, but the price can be far different than the guide price.

Green salamanders can be caught using a net trap in the Mort Myre Swamp south-east of Canifis. The hunting spot closest to the Canifis bank is just south-west of the Werewolf Agility Arena. This spot has 4 young trees close together, allowing you to set up 4 traps at once with 60 Hunter, using 4 small fishing nets and 4 ropes. To maximise the amount of lizards you bank per trip, you can leave your traps set up as you run to the bank rather than pick them all up and carry them with you. They will have fallen by the time you get back, so you will have to pick up the ropes and nets and reset the traps.
Note: There is a chance the ropes and nets will disappear if you take too long. It is important to stay focused when using this method.

Green salamanders can be difficult to catch at lower levels, therefore it is recommended to use a familiar that invisibly boosts your hunter level, such as a spirit larupia (level 57 Summoning) or an arctic bear (level 71 Summoning).

details:
One mahogany tree is located on the southwestern part of Ape Atoll next to the beach. Collect mahogany logs here, and run east to the bank deposit chest to bank the logs. The tree spawns unusually quickly, so it is worth waiting for it to respawn and gathering a full inventory rather than running all the way to the deposit chest after the tree falls.

Jungle spiders, poisonous jungle snakes and poisonous scorpions found throughout the jungle. Wearing a monkey greegree will keep the monsters from attacking, but it also takes up an inventory space for your hatchet unless the hatchet is stored on the tool belt. These monsters can be completely avoided if you run along the southern edge of the island in a direct line from the mahogany tree to the deposit chest.

There is approximately a 2.5% chance that you will cut a Special mahogany log. You can use two of these to convert an inventory of mahogany logs into mahogany planks, saving 19,500 coins per special log. On average you will get about ten of these per hour, which means you can convert 130 logs for free by talking to the sawmill operator. It takes about 40 seconds to turn a batch of logs into planks, which can be done at any time after amassing enough special mahogany logs.

* A Beaver gives an invisible Woodcutting boost of +2 which may give you more logs per minute. Beaver pouches are inexpensive, so it is worth it to use them. However their multichop special move does not work on Mahogany trees.
* An augmented hatchet with the honed perk increases the success of gathering logs by 2% per rank.
* A completed nature's sentinel outfit boosts woodcutting speed by 7% and also offers 20 daily teleports to tree locations.
* Any God banner can boost +2 visible woodcutting boost for 30 minutes once a day.
* Perfect juju woodcutting potion or perfect plus potion could increase log outcome by 5% every hour per dose (or 4 hours/dose with perfect plus).

Swamp toads can be picked up at the swamp northwest of the Grand Tree in the Tree Gnome Stronghold. There are 18 spawns, and it takes approximately 45 seconds for one to respawn on a high-populated world. Because of this, you will have to wait a few seconds after picking up all the toads before you can go through and pick them up again. After you have a full inventory, run east into the Grand Tree and southeast to the central tree with a ladder. There are two banks on the western part of the .

Toad's legs can be made by clicking on the swamp toads in your inventory, yielding per hour. The legs can be quickly pulled off on the run from the swamp to the bank. This usually lowers the value, so be sure to check the prices of both. Currently legs are worth  while the swamp toad itself is.

Sabre-toothed kyatt are found at the northern part of the Rellekka Hunter area. Create a pitfall trap by using one set of logs from a nearby dead tree with a knife on your tool belt. Click on one of the kyatt to tease them, which makes them attack and follow you around. Walk over to your set up pitfall trap with the kyatt right behind you and jump over it. The kyatt will either walk over it and fall in, or it will jump over as well. If it jumps over, set up a new trap at a new spot (they won't go over the same pitfall trap twice in a row) and repeat the process until the kyatt falls in. Collect a pair of big bones and either tatty kyatt fur or kyatt fur. If you get tatty fur, drop it and bury the bones, then continue to collect the non-tatty fur to sell on the Grand Exchange.

The quickest way to bank is with a charged TokKul-Zo to the Fight Caves, if you have completed The Elder Kiln. After banking at the Fight Caves, use the fairy ring to teleport south of the Feldip Hunter area. Run off the mountain then to the north over a small strip of land. Continue north until you reach the hunting area.

It is recommended to use the tree pitfall traps to the west on the non-snowy part of the hunter area. The kyatt spawn close to the traps and have a smaller walking range than those to the east. With a high Hunter level, you can continually catch the same kyatt right after it spawns if it never jumps over your traps.

Summoning familiars such as the spirit larupia, spirit graahk, and spirit kyatt (level 57 Summoning) or the arctic bear (level 71 Summoning) will invisibly boost your Hunter level, making it less likely that a kyatt will jump over your traps.

Spined larupia are found at the southern part of the Feldip Hunter area.    
Larupia are a consistent moneymaker due to the demand for their furs which are used in the creation of the Larupia outfit and Spirit larupia pouch.

# Create a pitfall trap by using one set of logs from a nearby jungle tree with a knife on your tool belt. 
# Click on one of the larupia to tease them using a teasing stick, which makes them attack and follow you around. 
# Walk over to your set up pitfall trap with the larupia right behind you and jump over it. The larupia will either walk over it and fall in, or it will jump over as well. If the larupia jumps over, set up a new trap at a new spot (they won't go over the same pitfall trap twice in a row) and repeat the process until the larupia falls in. 
# Collect a pair of big bones and either tatty larupia fur or larupia fur. If you get tatty fur, drop it and bury the bones, then continue to collect the non-tatty fur to sell on the Grand Exchange.

The quickest way to bank is with a charged TokKul-Zo to the Fight Caves, if you have completed The Elder Kiln. After banking at the Fight Caves, use the fairy ring  to teleport north of the Feldip Hunter area, then run south to the larupia hunting grounds.

It is recommended to use the southern-most pitfall trap near the red sandstone mine. One larupia spawns directly south of the southern-most trap, and another spawns directly west of the pitfall trap northwest of the southern one. With a high Hunter level, you can continually catch the same larupia right after it spawns if it never jumps over your traps.

Summoning familiars such as the spirit larupia, spirit graahk, and spirit kyatt (level 57 Summoning) or the arctic bear (level 71 Summoning) will invisibly boost your Hunter level, making it less likely that a larupia will jump over your traps. Alternatively, if you have completed As A First Resort, you can take a dip in the mud bath in Oo'glog to the south for a temporary 10% Hunter boost if you have a Hunter level of at least 48.

activity: Collecting swamp tar from the Lady Zay
image: Collecting swamp tar from the Lady Zay.png
input1note: I found that each barrel will only have 1 swamp paste each at a time. You will need to run back to each barrel over and over again.
details:
The Lady Zay has many barrels of swamp tar on its decks, which can be looted for substantial profit. Start out by using the Lunar Isle lodestone, and run to the docks and board the Lady Zay. Go down the stairs in the southern end of the ship, and you'll see four barrels of swamp tar. Go to one of them and start clicking on it until it's empty. Do the same for the other three barrels -- the amount of tar varies between 1 and at least 15, but it'll average about three per barrel. Head back to the first barrel you looted, waiting for the tar to spawn again, and start the cycle over again. It takes about 22 seconds for the tar to respawn and is not dependent on the population of the world.

The tar of course stacks, so you'll never have to bank. When you're finished, go to the Grand Exchange and sell the swamp tar, which shouldn't be too difficult as it's a high-volume item.

output4note: based on Armadyl battlestaff price
output5note: High alch and/or
details:
The profit rate assumes kills per hour. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed. It also assumes that you are killing Glacors in their cavern instead of at the Glacor front, as the Glacors at the front are significantly more difficult to kill due to there not being enough space to properly separate them from the enduring glacytes.

A guide on killing glacors can be found here. 95 Magic is highly recommended as fire spells provide increased accuracy and have a 1.5 times damage multiplier. 95 Prayer is recommended for access to soul split and torment, but players may get by with 92 Prayer. Access to Soul Split is nearly essential as much healing will be required, and having to bank several times per hour will reduce profit substantially. Additionally, glacors will respawn fast enough that only two or three different spawns need to be targeted. 

Killing glacors can be a decent mid-level money making method as they drop glacyte boots as well as shards of Armadyl, used to create the Armadyl battlestaff. Most drops are valuable and worth picking up. Nature runes are helpful to high alchemise some drops, such as dragon maces and rune equipment.

There are three snakes right next to the bank deposit chest north of Trouble Brewing on Mos Le'Harmless. These snakes always drop snake hide which is worth coins each. After obtaining an inventory full of snake hides, the hides may be deposited via the bank box. Each snake only has 250 life points, so they may be killed easily in one hit with a strong weapon. High level players will be able to kill upwards of 300 snakes per hour (1 snake every 10-12 seconds makes a full inventory every 5.5 minutes or so, resulting in around 313 snakes per hour minus the bank time).

Low level players should beware of aggressive jungle horrors which may be found near the western snake. You can minimise the time spent in their attack range by cycling your snake-killing from east-to-west (east snake, centre snake, west snake, repeat). However, this mainly applies to mages, as they will still be standing in the jungle horrors' range when killing the centre snake if cycling from west-to-east (although the horrors can still chase and hit melee players). If the jungle horrors inflict more damage than a player can handle, it is recommended to not kill the western snake in order to completely avoid the jungle horrors. If necessary, food and/or healing abilities should be used to maximise the number of kills per hour. If only killing two of the snakes, the number killed per hour will be significantly less, and therefore profit will be greatly reduced.

Optional: (Note: depending on your graphic settings, this tip may not apply to you)

The snakes, with their small, thin, yellow/brown, low-to-the-ground bodies, can often be hard to see among the tall grasses and green/brown ground of Mos Le'Harmless (especially the eastern-most snake, which spawns in a patch of tall grass). To make the snakes easier to see, you can customise your graphics settings to make the ground less detailed. Go to "Graphics settings", then "Custom". In this menu, toggle "Ground decorations" and "Textures" to "Off" (toggling "Textures" automatically toggles "Scenery Shadows" off as well). This makes it significantly easier to quickly spot the snakes by removing a lot of the grass, shadows, and other details that can obscure the ground. To spot the snakes even more quickly, you may wish to check the minimap for the yellow dot. Memorising the spot where each snake spawns helps significantly; if you can kill them fast enough, you can run up on each snake as it spawns, giving them no time to slither away.

Using the TokKul-Zo and fairy rings, you can make about 50 trips to the cosmic altar per hour. With 59 Runecrafting (giving double cosmic runes) and especially 75 Runecrafting (giving access to the giant pouch), this can be highly profitable.

Start out at the TzHaar Fight Cave bank in TzHaar City. Unload pure essence and store it in your pouches, then take out essence for your inventory. Run north and use the fairy ring to teleport to Zanaris. From there, run south to the agility shortcut -- if you have 66 Agility, go through both of them, although you may get stuck and take a small amount of damage before passing through. Run further south and enter the mysterious ruins, and then go directly to the altar. Craft your essence in your inventory and pouches, and then teleport back to the Fight Cave with your TokKul-Zo. If you are unwilling or unable to complete The Elder Kiln to gain the TokKul-Zo, it is possible to use the Wilderness Sword, starting at the Edgeville Bank and running across the river to the fairy ring there. This method is likely to be a little less efficient.

With this method you can craft about 2700 essence per hour, but without the giant pouch that will drop to about 2150. A massive pouch allows even more runes, although it requires 1,000 Runespan points and degrades into dust. In addition, the Infinity ethereal outfit can store 12 essence.

Completing Hero's Welcome will allow the player to make 5% more runes.

The profit rate assumes kills per hour. Your actual profits may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

Skogres and zogres can be found in Jiggig during and after the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest, and they always drop the ogre coffin keys that are used to loot ogre coffins. Since the bones from the coffins are quite valuable, the keys are valuable and skogres/zogres can be very worthwhile to kill. 

The undead ogres are located south of Castle Wars, in the main Jiggig area past the skull barrier. The easiest way to get here (and to bank) is by using the ring of duelling.

They are level 56 and only have 2000 life points, but there's a hitch -- unless you're using the ogre composite bow and brutal arrows, your damage will be reduced to 25% of what it would normally be. Since the ogre bow is a low-level weapon and brutal arrows can be difficult to obtain, it's often better to accept the reduction in damage and fight them with high-level, non-specialised items. Both monsters are weak to fire spells, but this seems to only give a boost in accuracy -- and since the creatures are low-level, you should generally be hitting 100% of the time regardless. Using melee is not recommended as the zogres/skogres have a long death animation and it's worth it to kill one, walk over to it, attack another one from a distance, and pick up the key once it shows up.

You should do this on a populated world, as the location is nearly always empty, and on low-population worlds the six monsters in the main pen may not respawn in time. It should only take 10-20 seconds to kill one even with the damage penalty, so a full inventory might take 8-10 minutes. Banking is very quick at Castle Wars. After you've finished, sell your keys on the Grand Exchange, but keep in mind that as ogre coffin keys have a low buying limit, you may be able to sell them in bulk for a higher price.

Alternatively, you could loot coffins with the keys you've obtained. This is more efficient since it saves banking time and can even be used between monster respawns. See Money making guide/Looting ogre coffins for more information.

Adamantite ore is an item that often sells for a high price, as it can be smelted in a furnace with a luminite ore to form an adamant bar, requiring level 40 Smithing.

There are several locations to mine adamantite, but one of the best places to mine adamantite is at the Rimmington mine (see page for banking details).

First, go to the ore locations and start mining. Once the player have a full inventory, go to the nearest bank, deposit the ores, return to the ore location, and repeat. The player may also find sedimentary geode while mining, which can increase the profit slightly. The player should also keep their stamina up, and mine any rockertunity the player may encounter, as it can increase the profit.

For a close approximation of ore mined per hour (of pure mining) based on your levels and gear see the mining rate calculator.

details:
The profit rate assumes kills per hour. Your actual profits may be higher or lower depending on your speed and luck.

The player is advised to use non-degradeable equipment whenever possible, as it eliminates the cost for repairing. As the drops aren't noted, the player are recommended to use magic notepaper in order to note the drops, saving time in the process. If the player want to use a bank, one can do so from Ashuelot Reis, however it requires a frozen key and forty zarosian killcount, or a set of ancient ceremonial robes in order to access the room she is located in.

Aviansies are found inside Armadyl's Eyrie in the God Wars Dungeon. See here for information on how to reach the God Wars Dungeon. Armadyl's Eyrie is the south-west part of the dungeon, and requires 70 Ranged to enter. Having a piece of Armadyl-affiliated clothing is strongly recommended, or else everything in the area will be aggressive toward you.

Aviansies have relatively low life points and may be quickly killed using threshold abilities. Every third aviansie can be used to build up adrenaline in order to quickly kill the next two with threshold abilities. Doing so can result in over 300 aviansies killed per hour.

Once you run out of food or you're finished, teleport out and sell your adamant stone spirits and other items on the Grand Exchange.

You can make money by casting Superheat Item on runite ore and luminite, turning it into rune bars. It's highly recommended to set up a bank preset with 13 runite ores, 13 luminite, and 13 nature runes. The preset should then be configured to be one of the two single-keypress buttons (which can be activated by pressing '1' and '2' respectively). With the addition of banks having "Load Last Preset from" by right clicking them, you can do this even more effectively. This allows players to cast superheat item almost continuously. With 57 Smithing there is a 10% chance for gaining 2 bars instead of 1 for the same amount of ore.

While it is possible to superheat over 1,815 bars in an hour, this is an incredibly click-intensive activity. To superheat even 1,716 bars in an hour requires near-undivided attention. Server latency/lag also has a significant impact on your output, as they impact the speed at which you can bank; use a world with low ping and low population count if possible.

The Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Onyx) spell enchants 10 bolts at a time, using one cosmic rune, one death rune and 20 fire runes. Use a staff of fire for free fire runes. Click the Enchant Crossbow Bolt magic spell, which opens a menu to enchant bolts. 60 sets of 10 bolts can be made using the menu, taking approximately 142 seconds. This gives a theoretical upper limit of 15,000 enchanted Onyx bolts per hour. As all inputs and outputs are stackable, there is no requirement to bank and this technique can be done anywhere.

If you prefer a more active method, it is possible using Tick manipulation to quadruple your profit and magic XP, by clicking on the Enchant Crossbow Bolt spell each Game tick, and confirming each click with your space bar. This method is high-intensity and is only maintanable over short periods of time, however it can be useful for clearing through your GE limit of bolts to fill Alchemiser mk. II.

The bolt market is fairly volatile, so test the profit of one set of bolts before you buy the runes and bolts in bulk. Maximise your profit by buying one Onyx bolt (e) instantly, and sell all of yours for slightly less than what you paid. They may take a while to sell, but an extra 100 coins per bolt can double your profit.

Mature grotworms are found in the bottom level of the Grotworm Lair, which can be accessed by either a long trek through the cave, or a shortcut requiring 50 Agility. Alternatively, players can teleport directly to the grotworms using Remora's necklace teleport after completing Song from the Depths. The grotworms are level 98 and have 12500 life points, so they are much harder to kill than they used to be. They are weak to bolts so it may be worth it to use Ranged against them, but a Magic weapon above level 70 (such as a Staff of light or Polypore staff) is also fairly effective. Consider using Soul Split or a bunyip, but the grotworms also drop two un-noted sharks commonly.

Mature grotworms drop adamant and rune very often. It's best to use High Level Alchemy on these drops to avoid banking too often. Alternatively, players can bring a spring cleaner. They also drop royal dragonhide and varying herbs and seeds uncommonly. If you pick up all these items, you'll generally have to bank about once per hour.

The warped bats in the Lumbridge Catacombs drop batwing about 25% of the time. They are quite easy to kill fast, as they only have 600 life points and respawn almost instantly. Using a two-handed weapon to maximise the initial auto-attack, use basic abilities like Wrack or Piercing Shot to kill them if the first hit isn't enough. Pick up any batwing, and teleport back with the Lumbridge lodestone, bank, and repeat.

location: Ogre island south-west of Yanille lodestone
details:
Four jangerberries, used to make zamorak brews, can be found on an ogre-infested island north of Gu'Tanoth. The berries respawn about as fast as you can collect them, and since they are currently worth coins, collecting them can be fairly profitable.

Starting at the Castle Wars lobby with only a rope in your inventory and a ring of duelling equipped, run straight east to the island. Use Surge to either cross the bridge or after the point where the character last turns before the lake to speed up the trip. Then, use the rope on the tree branch, jumping over to the island (this will use up the rope). 

The ogres on the island are not aggressive. Run in a circle, continually collecting the berries. When your inventory is full, teleport back to the lobby with your duelling ring, bank, and repeat. A bank preset can be used to speed banking up.

activity: Tanning Royal dragonhide with Make Leather
other:
* spell unlocked from Livid Farm (75,000 produce points)
* Lunar spellbook active
location: Grand Exchange or bank chest recommended
details:
Royal dragon leather is used to train Crafting, and it is always in high demand. Because Royal dragonhide must be tanned into leather before it can be crafted, tanning the hides in bulk can be highly profitable.

While regular tanning can be quite profitable on its own, using the lunar spell Make Leather (which tans five hides at once) can increase the profit by more than 50% while also giving decent Magic experience. The downside is that Make Leather must be unlocked from Livid Farm, which requires 75,000 produce points.

Because the price difference between hides and leather can be fairly small, it is important to buy the hides for a low price and sell the leather for a high price; you can lose out on much of the profit or even turn a loss if you are not patient. Test the profit by buying one Royal dragonhide and one Royal dragon leather. If the difference between the two is less than 200, it may be worth it to switch to a different hide type. In some cases the profit can be more than 500 coins -- the guide prices on the Grand Exchange are not always indicative of the current trading price.

Begin by equipping your staff of fire and withdrawing body runes and astral runes, along with 26 royal dragonhides. Click the Make Leather spell (either in the spellbook or directly on your action bar) and use it on one of the hides. Bank your royal dragon leather and repeat. With fast banking, one can make a total of 26,000 leathers an hour. A Large rune pouch can be used to further increase hides per hour.

When finished, sell the leather on the Grand Exchange. Since the margin can be rather high, consider buying one royal dragon leather first and selling yours for one coin below that. This can save you more than 100 coins per item.

The profit rate assumes kills per hour. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

After completing Forgiveness of a Chaos Dwarf you can access the Chaos Dwarf Battlefield, filled with dwarves that drop the dragon pickaxe. It is recommended to use Magic due to the monsters' low life points, and multicombat abilities.

The dwarves and cannoneers are not very powerful, and they only have 1,000 and 2,500 life points, respectively. They get killed very quickly, so it's almost unnecessary to use threshold and ultimate abilities. However, you will want to use multicombat abilities like Chain, Dragon Breath and Tsunami, as the dwarves will crowd you and you can hit many of them at once. Sunshine can also be used to boost your damage. Try to avoid the chaos dwogres, as they will slow you down.

Try to hit the dwarves as fast as you can; the nearby Black Guard crossbowdwarfs left alive will easily decimate the chaos dwarves almost immediately. Due to attacking a chaos dwarf, nearby chaos dwarves will start to attack you. Although they do not hit very accurately, the damage will quickly stack up. To avoid this, you should have prayer restoring neck-wear like the demon horn necklace, a bonecrusher, and Soul Split to recover from your battle wounds. If you do not, you may want to use protection prayers, and occasionally use Ice Asylum or Elite Enhanced Excalibur.

With recommended stats and prayers, and effective use of multi-target abilities, you should be able to kill about 520 monsters per hour. A focused player with max stats and high level equipment (such as augmented Anima Core), Sunshine, and Soulsplit (with Bonecrusher and Twisted Bird Skull Necklace+) can expect to kill up to 1250 monsters per hour, which will result in a Pickaxe drop once every ~4 hours on average, massively increasing the profit per hour.

There are only a few drops worth picking up -- the dragon pickaxe has a drop chance of 1/5,000, so in the very long run you should get about one pickaxe per eight hours if you kill them in equal amounts. They also drop hand cannon shot, 100 at a time, which is also worth picking up as well as Muddy keys. Due to their demand in Invention, the Hand cannons dropped are also worth a good amount. Other than that, both monsters give access to the rare drop table so it is worth wearing a Ring of Wealth, even though it does not increase the chances of receiving a dragon pickaxe. Using a charming imp to pick up the charms they drop can give you about 100 gold, 40 green, 25 crimson and 20 blue charms per hour.

The profit rate assumes trips per hour. Your actual profit may be higher or lower depending on your speed.

Using the War's Retreat Teleport to bank, then teleporting to Lunar Island with Moonclan Teleport is the optimal way to craft astral runes. Players can do approximately 100 runs per hour via this method by using surge and dive during runs. Without teleporting, the number of runs per hour drops significantly, to approximately 60.

With the infinity ethereal outfit, an abyssal titan summoned, small through massive pouches and a powerburst of sorcery, players can hold up to 102 essence per trip. Players should put the runes needed for Moonclan Teleport in a large rune pouch to save inventory space. 

Create a preset with all the required items for your trips. Pouches can be filled by loading the preset. After filling your pouches and ethereal set, run outside the Lunar Isle wall, south then east past the suqahs. Once at the astral altar, craft your runes and then teleport to War's Retreat. Fill your pouches again, then cast Moonclan Teleport and begin anew.

If you do not have an War's Retreat Teleport, you could cast Moonclan Teleport and use the Lunar Isle bank; however this is slightly slower. The lodestone teleport is also an option, however this is not recommended due to the large delay when casting it.

If the player does not have the expansive pouch, then it is recommended to have the Pouch Protector relic active, as it prevents pouches from degrading. Alternatively, players can cast the Repair Rune Pouch spell unlocked from Livid Farm—or NPC Contact spell to contact the dark mage—to repair pouches as they degrade if the relic is not unlocked or if all three monolith slots are filled.

If you have a second preset with the runes to cast the NPC contact spell and use a hotkey to activate the spell, you can cut down on the amount of time spent repairing pouches if the relic or pouch protect spells are not options for you. A free method of repairing pouches would be to traverse into the abyss and speak with the dark mage in person. As the abyss is in the wilderness, players should proceed on this route with caution.

You can use a bank preset with a combined Catalyst fragment plus Infinity ethereal outfit to prevent medium, large and giant pouches from degrading if you do not have  the Pouch Protector relic unlocked.

Completing Hero's Welcome will allow players to craft 5% more runes.
